findings.description: ticksPerSecond is used as a divisor; if configured to 0 (or negative), this will crash.
Casting double damagePerTick to int may overflow and is undefined behavior if the value is out of range.
The loop simulates time by incrementing elapsedTimeSeconds but never sleeps; it will peg the CPU.
cooldownSeconds, durationSeconds, and damagePerTick are not validated; negative/NaN values break logic and may create infinite loops or unexpected behavior.
With invalid ability parameters (e.g., zero/negative duration/cooldown), abilities might never deal damage, causing a potential infinite loop.
Time-of-check vs time-of-use pattern by calling canDealDamage twice per tick, potentially inconsistent decisions if state changes (future concurrent refactor).
Public mutable health permits untrusted mutation.
